Plot an LPPLS calibration

Source: R/lppls_fitter.R
plot.lppls_fit.Rd

Returns one of the plots attached to the fit, or draws one on demand. The attached ones exist only if they were asked for at fit time (fp, pp, mp, tp, mpl_plot, cp, sp). "basin", "param_basin" and "mpl_relative" are drawn from what the fit stores anyway, so they need nothing asked for in advance.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'lppls_fit'
plot(
  x,
  which = c("basin", "param_basin", "fit", "mpl", "mpl_relative", "param", "matrix",
    "trace_mo", "trace_bm", "trace_bo", "contour", "surface"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An object of class "lppls_fit" from fit_lppls().

which

Which plot to return. "basin", "param_basin" and "mpl_relative" are drawn on demand; the rest are returned from the fit.

...

Ignored.

Value

A ggplot2 object (a plotly object for "contour"/"surface").

Details

"basin" plots each fit's SSE against its tc, split at the gap print.lppls_fit() reports. When a search has failed on part of the grid the two clusters separate visibly, which is invisible in the point estimate.

"param_basin" is the per-tc parameter plot with the same split applied to every parameter, not just the objective. It answers what "basin" cannot: which parameters the inferior fits differ in – typically omega jumping between local optima while m stays pinned at its bound.

"mpl_relative" draws the modified profile likelihood relative to its maximum, \(R = \log \mathrm{MPL} - \max \log \mathrm{MPL}\), zoomed to the band the likelihood-interval cutoffs live in, with each cutoff drawn as a horizontal line. The absolute level of the log MPL carries no information, whereas \(R\) is what the intervals test, so each interval can be read off where the curve crosses its cutoff. It needs a fit made with mode = "MPL".

See also

fit_lppls(), print.lppls_fit()
